record.oneLiner: A giant sail-backed, semiaquatic fish-eating theropod.
record.description: Spinosaurus was among the largest known terrestrial carnivores, with a long, low, narrow crocodile-like skull bearing straight conical teeth, robust clawed forelimbs, short legs, and a paddle-like tail. Its trademark neural spines, over 1.65 m long, likely supported a skin sail. It lived in Cretaceous North Africa and ate both aquatic and terrestrial prey.

notableFacts.text: Its tall neural spines (over 1.65 m) likely supported a skin sail.
Ate both aquatic and terrestrial prey, with a crocodile-like snout.
The original 1912 remains were destroyed in World War II; new material emerged in the 21st century.
